description: A collaborative team passionate about space, science, technology, and education. We aim to build an engaging interactive experience that makes real space-mission challenges understandable and fun for young learners. Looking for teammates skilled in programming, game development, space science, physics, biology, UI/UX, data, or storytelling. Curiosity and teamwork matter more than experience!
summary:
.Lunar Outpost: The Last Frontier is an interactive lunar mission-training game designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of establishing and maintaining a human outpost beyond Earth.

Players explore an isometric lunar environment, complete mission objectives, interact with infrastructure, and manage simulated life-support resources. Across five missions, they learn about habitat operations, solar power, greenhouse food production, rover exploration, crew safety, radiation research, and long-term outpost sustainability.

The project includes a NASA OSDR RadLab research panel presenting comparison statistics for two Artemis I radiation instruments. It distinguishes actual scientific comparison results from simulated gameplay values and makes clear that the observations are not direct lunar-surface measurements.

By combining exploration, resource management, and educational mission scenarios, the game aims to make the complexities of space exploration more understandable and engaging for younger learners.
details:
Lunar Outpost: The Last Frontier is an interactive 2D isometric lunar outpost simulation created as a junior astronaut mission-training experience.

Players control an astronaut, explore the lunar environment, interact with outpost structures, and complete objectives across five missions. The game introduces important concepts involved in sustaining a human presence beyond Earth, including habitat operations, power generation, greenhouse food production, life-support resource management, rover exploration, crew safety, and radiation research.

The game features interactive infrastructure, mission objectives, resource indicators, environmental details, and scenario-based challenges. Players must make decisions while balancing simulated resources and responding to mission events.

A dedicated NASA RadLab research panel in Level 4 presents an absorbed-dose-rate comparison between Artemis-I-EAD-MU01 and Artemis-I-M42-SN127. It displays the supplied comparison period, regression relationship, and R² statistic. The panel clearly identifies these as Artemis I instrument observations, not direct lunar-surface measurements. Raw per-reading data has not been imported, and all gameplay exposure values and resource penalties are identified as simulation assumptions.

The project was developed using MakePlay.ai with assistance from ChatGPT for research, planning, prompt development, and AI-assisted implementation. The team considered educational accessibility, scientific accuracy, resource-management concepts, gameplay clarity, and the limitations of representing real space environments through a simplified simulation.

The intended impact is to help younger learners explore the scientific, operational, and decision-making challenges of future lunar missions through an engaging interactive experience.
